Domain Kernel Tour¶

From dense sources to a reusable legislative model¶

Main journey: 60–90 minutes. Advanced exercises are optional and stay in this notebook.

You are a developer at a lobbying organisation. Your colleagues want to analyse new legislation for clients working with AI in recruitment. The relevant language is spread across an EU regulation, Commission guidance, stakeholder papers and existing ontologies. You need to understand what a system is intended to do, who holds responsibilities, and what information or safeguards the legislation describes. The same word can carry different meanings; a useful application needs those meanings to be explicit and traceable.

Your task here is to build the application's domain model: named concepts, relationships, data shapes, evidence and reviewed mappings. Domain Kernel supplies that reusable contract. Your downstream application will perform legislative analysis and produce client intelligence.

Live SDK steps in C1, C2, C7, E6, E9 and R1. Open the scoped recruitment model, review its first vocabulary and inspect authored shapes. Later operations are labelled simulations. The source ledger records how each source was verified.

The result tables contain concrete mock records: stable example IDs, meanings, citations, checks and decisions. Actor IDs and timestamps are fictional. Tables select useful fields for inspection; they do not define a new serialization format. The original EN and FR AI Act PDFs are verified. Any unavailable advanced resource remains visibly unverified; its simulated output is not a claim of acquisition or engine execution.

Before you begin¶

You should be comfortable reading Python objects, lists and async/await. You do not need prior ontology experience or knowledge of the AI Act. The source ledger supplies the selected passages; this tutorial teaches how to preserve and review their meanings, not how to give legal advice.

You will finish with a portable contract another developer can inspect without your database. Use it to supply definitions, data shapes, reviewed reference links and evidence to your own application. The short destination preview below shows that handoff before you build it.

How to use this notebook¶

Open this repository folder in VS Code. Install the notebook group with uv sync --locked --group notebook, select the repository's .venv kernel, then choose Run All. Environment provisioning is separate; execution needs no credentials or live services. The configured notebook working directory is the repository root.

Read the primary result in each chapter first. Expand Inspect supporting detail when you want the diagnostics, and use the optional source/model controls for deeper inspection. C9 includes a complete evidence-to-contract example and a read-only consumer exercise.

Read the canonical walkthrough first. Explore selections are read-only and update immediately. For a sample change, choose an alternative, explain it, preview its impact and explicitly apply it. Experiments are separate from the fixed storyline, so rejecting a suggestion will not quietly change the examples further down.

The commented code shows upcoming SDK operations. The labelled preview snapshots show their expected results. Run C1 to pin the source, then inspect the live authored shapes in C7, E6 and R1.

In C6–C7, pause at Your turn to make a choice or find a lookup name. Check your answer gives local teaching feedback; it never submits an SDK decision. Hints and worked answers are available when needed, including expandable answers in the saved reading version.

Kernel restart rebuilds this preview. Re-running an ordinary cell preserves its current experiment. Reset experiment resets only that branch; no real database or user data is touched.

What you will hand to another developer¶

Your application needs more than a list of terms. For example, it needs to distinguish instructions for deployers from technical documentation, describe the information those instructions contain, and retain the conditions attached to that information.

Look ahead to the final simulated publication 1.1.0 below. The consumer can find a definition by name and inspect its field shape. A separate descriptive rule carries the logging qualification and its citation. The form or extraction workflow using that contract remains your application's responsibility. This preview reads a fixed final sample; it does not advance your working model.

The planned consumer code — we will return to it in C9 
instructions = consumer.get_concept(name="instructions-for-use")
logging = instructions.get_attribute(name="logging-mechanisms")
print(instructions.display_name)
print(logging.name, logging.required, logging.collection)

Here, consumer is the bundle loaded with DomainModelBundle.deserialize(payload=portable). C9 will show that complete handoff and retrieve the separate rule.

The objects you will work with¶

Object Meaning in this journey
Project The workspace grouping your models and sources.
Model Your evolving domain definitions; this is not a language model.
Concept A reusable type such as AI provider, not a particular company.
Change plan A proposed set of edits, built before submission.
Review case A proposal and the decisions required to resolve it.
Publication An immutable released snapshot of the reviewed model.
Bundle The portable model contract your application can consume.
Evidence A captured source reference and locator supporting a proposed meaning.
Ontology A published vocabulary with stable identifiers and explicit semantic relationships.

You will move through draft → reviewed working model → published snapshot → consumer. A generated id preserves identity, a name supports exact lookup, and a display_name is the readable label. For example, Instructions for use has the name instructions-for-use. Editing its label does not generate a new identity; a reviewed change produces a new revision.

In C1, ModelKind.OBSERVED says that you are describing an existing domain. It does not mean that a definition has been approved. Review status is a separate concern.

C1 · Start a workspace¶

You are building legislative-analysis software for a lobbying organisation whose clients use AI in recruitment. Your colleagues can read the Act, but the application needs stable meanings it can reuse: what a system is intended to do, who is responsible, and what documentation or safeguards the legislation describes. Those meanings must stay connected to their sources when new evidence arrives.

Your first task is to set that modelling boundary around recruitment and selection. Choose the English text of the original Official Journal edition of 12 July 2024 from the source manifest. A later legal edition would be a separate input revision.

Live SDK · Set the scope and pin the source. ContentHash checks the spelling of the recorded digest for the original PDF bytes. If the pin is missing or invalid, restore the verified ai-act-en entry in fixtures/sources.json. The original PDF is provisioned for ingestion in C3.

    raise ValueError(msg)

source_hash = ContentHash(value=f"sha256:{source.sha256}")
model_kind = ModelKind.OBSERVED
model_name = "ai-in-recruitment"
model_display_name = "AI in recruitment"
model_description = (
    "Cover recruitment and selection, actor responsibilities, documentation and safeguards. "
    "Preserve legal qualifications and distinguish legislation from stakeholder positions."
)

_ = sys.stdout.write(
    f"{model_display_name} ({model_kind.value})\n"
    f"Planned model lookup name {model_name}\n"
    f"{model_description}\n"
    f"{source.edition}\n"
    f"{source_hash.value}\n"
)

The digest pins one source edition. The model's lookup name is how you will reopen the model in its project, and the SDK will generate a separate permanent model ID when you create it. ModelKind.OBSERVED records your intent to describe an existing domain. Approval requires an explicit review decision.

Create or reopen the recruitment project and model in the demo workspace. Default SQLite initialises on the first awaited database operation. Keep the same demo name to resume. To start fresh, choose an unused demo name such as recruitment-fresh. Selecting a name leaves existing demo and application data intact.

Manual authoring uses no gateway. Configuration inspection reports the settings origin and who owns initialisation. Use Client(config="domain-kernel.toml") for a selected TOML file. A Python ClientConfiguration(base_dir=...) selects an isolated location with the same default database behavior. A configured database selects an operator-prepared database.

The scope now tells a future reader what this model is for. You have not classified any client system. Next, establish a small reviewed vocabulary so you can assess what discovery adds rather than accepting every proposed term.

Implementation ownership

DK-001 supplies the live scope step. DK-003 supplies SQLite transactions. DK-004 supplies create and reopen operations. DK-020 supplies local file ingestion.

Check your understanding. Does OBSERVED mean that the model is approved?

Reveal the explanation

No. It describes the modelling intent. A proposal still needs review, and a reviewed working model still needs publication.

C2 · Publish the first model¶

You have a workspace and a scope, but no reusable vocabulary yet. Begin with three meanings you can explain: a recruitment AI system, its provider and its deployer. The system meaning is deliberately narrower than the Act's general AI-system definition. Giving it the explicit name recruitment-ai-system prevents that restriction from disappearing behind a generic label.

You will author the three definitions and their relationships, inspect the proposed changes, accept them and publish a first bundle. Starting manually gives you a small contract against which to judge discovery later. It also shows that documents and inference are optional ways to grow the model, not prerequisites for using the SDK.

These are definitions of types, not records of particular companies or products. Separate provider and deployer meanings do not imply that a company cannot occupy both roles. Likewise, the permissive many-to-many relationship shape below is an application modelling choice, not a cardinality prescribed by the Act.

Propose the first business meanings¶

Use the pinned English edition's Article 3 definitions when writing the narrower recruitment meaning and its two actor roles. These drafts are application-authored meanings. The source passages guide the author. Evidence ingestion and linked source records arrive in C3.

Submit three intended concepts and an alternate concept for the scripted reviewer to decline. The request keys let the same demo workspace reopen the original proposals when you rerun.

In [7]:
system_passage = next(passage for passage in source.passages if passage.id == "ai-3-system")
actor_passage = next(passage for passage in source.passages if passage.id == "ai-3-actors")
draft_meanings = [
    (
        "Recruitment AI system",
        "An AI system used to screen applications or evaluate candidates in recruitment.",
        system_passage.locator,
    ),
    (
        "AI provider",
        "An actor placing a developed or commissioned AI system on the market under its name.",
        actor_passage.locator,
    ),
    (
        "AI deployer",
        "An actor using a system under its authority in a professional context.",
        actor_passage.locator,
    ),
    (
        "Screening service",
        "Any service involved in recruitment screening.",
        system_passage.locator,
    ),
]
leaf_cases = []
for display_name, meaning, locator in draft_meanings:
    leaf_cases.append(
        await model.propose_definition(
            actor="demo:developer",
            display_name=display_name,
            meaning=meaning,
            body=ConceptDefinition(),
            reason=f"Authored for this application alongside {locator}.",
            idempotency_key=f"c2-propose-{display_name}",
        )
    )
_ = sys.stdout.write(
    f"Proposals recorded: {len(leaf_cases)}\n"
    f"Authoring references: {system_passage.locator} and {actor_passage.locator}\n"
)

Proposals recorded: 4
Authoring references: Article 3(1); PDF page 46 and Article 3(3)–(4); PDF page 46

Preview the decisions¶

Inspect each pending case and its effects. An accepted case on a resumed run already has a durable decision. The first run displays the reviewed additions before any become active.

In [8]:
review_actions = [
    *[Accept(reason="The meaning fits the recruitment policy model.") for _ in leaf_cases[:3]],
    Reject(reason="This service category is broader than the intended AI-system scope."),
]
active_before_review = (await model.list_definitions()).items
pending_impacts = []
for original_case, action in zip(leaf_cases, review_actions, strict=True):
    pending_case = await model.get_review_case(case_id=original_case.id)
    if pending_case.status is CaseStatus.PENDING:
        pending_impacts.append(await model.preview_changes(case=pending_case, decision=action))
previewed_additions = sum(len(impact.definition_changes) for impact in pending_impacts)
_ = sys.stdout.write(
    f"Prospective additions: {previewed_additions}\n"
    f"Active definitions before review: {len(active_before_review)}\n"
)

Prospective additions: 3
Active definitions before review: 0

Record the reviewed decisions¶

Run All uses the scripted sample reviewer to accept three concepts and reject the broader screening service in a separate decision. Applications submit only after their own reviewer inspects the cases. The accepted vocabulary is now in the working model.

In [9]:
receipts = []
for original_case, action in zip(leaf_cases, review_actions, strict=True):
    receipts.append(
        await model.decide_review(
            actor="demo:reviewer",
            case=original_case,
            decision=action,
            idempotency_key=f"c2-decision-{original_case.id.value}",
        )
    )
system = await model.get_concept(name="recruitment-ai-system")
active_after_review = (await model.list_definitions()).items
declined_names = {"screening-service"}.isdisjoint(
    definition.name for definition in active_after_review
)
_ = sys.stdout.write(
    f"Reviewed definition: {system.name} ({system.kind.value})\n"
    f"Active definitions after review: {len(active_after_review)}\n"
    f"Alternate proposal remains inactive: {declined_names}\n"
)

Extend the reviewed vocabulary with relationships¶

Reload after the leaf decisions so the builder pins the inspected workspace revision. Pass the loaded definitions directly to the two relationship operations. Inspect the plan and its coordinated case before recording a separate decision.

In [10]:
async def existing_demo_plan(*, workspace: Model, reason: str) -> ModelChangePlan | None:
    """Find the unchanged plan from a prior run of this isolated teaching workspace."""
    cases = await workspace.list_review_cases(kind=CaseKind.CHANGE_SET)
    return next((case.change_plan for case in cases.items if case.reason == reason), None)


model = await project.get_model(name=model_name)
graph_reason = "Connect the reviewed provider and deployer roles to the recruitment system."
graph_plan = await existing_demo_plan(workspace=model, reason=graph_reason)
if graph_plan is None:
    system = await model.get_concept(name="recruitment-ai-system")
    provider = await model.get_concept(name="ai-provider")
    deployer = await model.get_concept(name="ai-deployer")
    graph_builder = DomainModelBuilder(model_info=model.info)
    graph_builder.add_relationship(
        display_name="Provides",
        meaning="The provider makes a recruitment AI system available.",
        source=provider,
        target=system,
        cardinality=RelationshipCardinality.many_to_many(),
    )
    graph_builder.add_relationship(
        display_name="Uses",
        meaning="A deployer uses a recruitment AI system.",
        source=deployer,
        target=system,
        cardinality=RelationshipCardinality.many_to_many(),
    )
    graph_plan = graph_builder.build_change_plan(reason=graph_reason)
_ = sys.stdout.write(
    f"Planned relationships: {', '.join(item.content.name for item in graph_plan.operations)}\n"
    f"Active definitions before plan submission: {len((await model.list_definitions()).items)}\n"
)

Planned relationships: provides, uses
Active definitions before plan submission: 3

graph_decision = Accept(reason="Both relationships bind to the intended reviewed actor and system.")
if graph_case.status is CaseStatus.PENDING:
    graph_impact = await model.preview_changes(case=graph_case, decision=graph_decision)
    _ = sys.stdout.write(f"Coordinated preview: {len(graph_impact.definition_changes)} additions\n")
else:
    _ = sys.stdout.write("Coordinated case already reviewed\n")

C3 · Parse the evidence¶

You have published a small vocabulary describing recruitment AI systems, providers and deployers. That gives your application a consistent starting point, but it cannot yet describe the information a provider supplies or the safeguards associated with using a system.

Those details are spread across several provisions. Before proposing more definitions, you need evidence that you can inspect and return to during review. Ingest the selected legislation and guidance, then examine their structure and individual passages. The English and French original OJ PDFs have now been acquired and checked; their byte hashes and exact locations are recorded in the source ledger.

Parsing gives you addressable evidence; it does not decide what the model should contain. Keep the document identity, edition and passage location together. You will also inspect a deliberately broken third input: the two successful documents remain useful even though that file cannot be parsed. In the next chapter, this evidence will support proposed meanings, making it possible to distinguish a parsing error from a modelling disagreement.

Inputs for this step. The default inputs reader resolves files below the configured base directory. Before enabling these SDK calls, provision ai-act.pdf and guidance.pdf from the hash-verified acquisitions, plus the intentionally malformed broken-demo.pdf. The active preview uses the local source ledger, so Run All never downloads or parses these files.

You can follow a passage back to its edition and page, and distinguish the broken input from successful evidence. That is the foundation for reviewing proposals. Next, inspect how discovery turns several passages into a richer model without changing the accepted seed.

No. Parsing supplies inspectable evidence. Discovery proposes meanings and review decides what enters the model. The failed third file does not erase the two successful inputs.

C4 · Discover meanings¶

Your evidence is now addressable, so you can ask for proposed domain meanings. You supplied the full original AI Act, not an Article 13 extract. Your application needs a recruitment model, not an inventory of every sector covered by the Act. The model description gives discovery its persistent context; additional instructions let you state the focus of this particular run.

You will ask for recruitment uses, responsibilities and safeguards while preserving relevant definitions and qualifications wherever they appear. This is how you guide the proposals toward your use case without hiding cross-references from the extractor. It is guidance, not a hard page filter: inspect what a live run includes and misses rather than expecting the fixture list exactly. The selected passages in this preview are a reviewed teaching/evaluation rubric.

The useful result is more than a list of nouns. Article 13 can suggest fields for instructions for use; Articles 10 and 26 distinguish development data from deployer-controlled input data; Article 6 contributes qualifications that a simple high-risk label would lose.

Inspect the proposal groups before looking at the graph. The graph still shows the accepted seed: discovery has not earned the right to change it. The detailed instructions proposal below shows the kind of information you should expect to review—field shapes, the passage supporting each field, and whether its structure is inferred or chosen for the application.

Two deliberately flawed suggestions make the review work concrete. One treats every recruitment system as equivalent to a high-risk recruitment system. Another conflates instructions for use with technical documentation. A correctly shaped inference response can still contain either mistake. A separate failed guidance segment is also visible; successful proposals, failures and unresolved questions are different parts of the run.

Tell discovery what you are building¶

With neither option, discovery uses the SDK default and your model context. For this journey, use additional_instructions: it keeps that default and adds your recruitment brief. You do not need to write a complete extraction prompt or repeat the output schema. The sample capture below makes the baseline visible; the next operation shows the added focus and its proposed meanings.

Try a narrower brief in an independent branch¶

Suppose you want a second pass concerned only with documentation. A full prompt_override lets you supply that instruction text yourself. This experiment copies the seed publication into a separate model and keeps the same evidence revisions; it does not replace the main run or its pending queue. Supplying both arguments here is deliberate: the override wins, so the default and additional_instructions are ignored. Normally, you would pass just the override.

Your freedom concerns the instructions. The SDK still sends its fixed ModelRequest.response_schema_json, supplies model context/evidence separately and validates responses. The existing failed-segment example still appears in run.failures; existing bounded retry and recovery behavior is unchanged. An override cannot make an invalid response acceptable, and recovery does not silently substitute the default prompt.

Compare the two captures, especially which meanings are now in focus. A narrower brief must still retain conditions and cross-references needed to interpret them. It is not evidence that everything outside the brief is legally irrelevant, nor that the exact displayed proposals will be reproduced.

HANDS-ON PRACTICE

Your turn: focus discovery without changing its contract

Your experiment supplies recruitment_focus and a documentation-only prompt_override. Decide which instructions reach the gateway and what happens if a response does not fit the proposal schema.

  1. Effective instructions: Default + additional + override / Override only / Additional instructions only
  2. Response outside the SDK proposal schema: Accept a caller-defined response shape / Keep SDK validation and failure handling / Silently retry with the default prompt

Evidence: ai-13-instructions, ai-6-classification. Use the controls below, or write down your answers in the reading version.

Worked answer and explanations

Worked answer

  • override: Only the override is used. The default and additional instructions are ignored; evidence and model context remain separate inputs.
  • validate: The SDK still validates its fixed schema and uses the existing failure, bounded retry and recovery behavior. A prompt cannot make invalid output valid.
prompt_override takes precedence.
ModelRequest.response_schema_json stays SDK-owned.
Inspect run.failures and pending cases separately.

You can change what discovery looks for while keeping proposals consumable by review and publication. This feedback does not run discovery, alter source selection or submit decisions.

run.prompt records the effective instructions and versions used. A retry or resume_discovery(run_id=...) reuses that capture, so you do not need to reconstruct the brief. A changed brief starts a new run; reusing a request key with changed arguments is a conflict. New discovery calls do not inherit the previous run's additional instructions. In C10 you will pass the recruitment focus again when introducing stakeholder evidence; E9 shows resumption.

Return now to the main recruitment run. None of this branch's proposals has been accepted or added to it. Your next task is to compare the main proposals with reusable ontology meanings.

Try it: Inspect instructions-for-use fields. Check whether the proposed fields retain the source qualifications.

The proposal card contains useful field-level detail, but it is still an authored expected result. In a real run, evidence quality and reviewer corrections would determine whether discovery saved work. Before deciding, compare these local meanings with existing ontologies.

C5 · Reuse ontologies¶

You now have local proposals, but you do not need to invent every meaning yourself. Existing vocabularies can supply recognisable identities, definitions and relationships. ELI helps describe legislative resources and their representations. DPV's AI Act extension includes instructions for use, technical documentation, intended purpose and assessments.

Reuse still requires judgement. Compare each term with the local definition and the legal edition you selected. The vocabulary's recruitment high-risk category is attractive, but an equivalence would overstate what you know about a local concept that includes all recruitment AI systems. The general AI-system term is a better broader reference for that local scope.

Inspect the original IRIs and the selected resource versions. Loading a resource, recording a business mapping and adopting formal axioms are separate operations. The selected DPV resource also retains a provisional-agreement note on one term: that is a reason to inspect source quality, not to silently discard the original identity or assume every term is current.

Think of an ontology as a shared vocabulary whose terms have stable web identities. Matching a local label to a label elsewhere is not enough: inspect their meanings and retain the selected relationship. A consumer can then recognise that your local recruitment meaning is narrower than the external general AI-system term without relying on a string match.

Inputs for this step. eli_document is the pinned ELI OntologyDocument; eli_resources contains its explicitly supplied dependency documents. The selected DPV resources are listed in the source ledger. Supplying those typed assets is a host boundary, not a hidden network fetch. This optional adoption plan is pending; the main model is still the C2 seed. C6 reviews the business alignments separately. Formal axiom adoption and dependency closure are explored further in E1.

Check your understanding. Does a narrower-than reference mapping make two definitions interchangeable?

Reveal the explanation

No. It records a direction between meanings and retains both identities. A reviewed business mapping also does not automatically assert OWL equivalence.

C6 · Reconcile meanings¶

You have proposals from the documents and candidate meanings from the reference packs. Your next job is to decide which distinctions the application should retain. A plausible label is not enough: merging two meanings can remove a qualification the application will later need.

Work through three questions: what stays distinct, what a source phrase refers to, and how a local meaning compares with a reference. Each short operation shows its own result. You will practise the decisions before the chapter assembles the accepted model.

1 · Keep different meanings distinct¶

Start with the suggested equivalence between recruitment AI and high-risk recruitment AI. Revisit the Article 6 qualifications preserved in C4. Rejecting blanket equivalence records a decision; it does not delete either definition or decide the status of a particular organisation.

Where the selected case identities come from

These are illustrative opaque IDs, not production constants or queue positions. Your host UI carries the selected returned ID into get_review_case().

3 · Compare the local meaning with a reference¶

Now change the question. You are comparing the scope of two definitions: your recruitment concept and the general AI-system meaning selected from DPV. Read the relation from local to reference. The local concept includes an extra recruitment restriction, so its scope is smaller.

reference_case is the selected reference-alignment case; reference_system is the pinned external ReferenceDefinition inspected in C5. It is not the local ai-system concept. Try the direction yourself before reading the planned call.

Worked answer

  • mapping: The reviewed mapping retains two identities and a direction; it does not add a formal OWL assertion.

    reference_definition=reference_system,
    reason="The local recruitment scope is narrower.",
)

Check your understanding. Why can the source mapping use same_as() while the reference mapping uses narrower_than()?

Reveal the explanation

The source case resolves one occurrence to its local meaning. The reference case compares the scope of two definitions. A recruitment occurrence can use the local recruitment meaning while that meaning remains narrower than the general AI-system reference.

C7 · Refine the model¶

You have a reviewed vocabulary. Now make it useful to the developer building forms or extracting facts with it. You will refine one capture shape, preserve its qualification, repair an identity assumption and review the changes together.

Keep one builder throughout this chapter. Each early cell adds to its draft; none changes the accepted model until the final decision is submitted. The small outputs show the intended draft result, not a sequence of silently accepted revisions.

1 · Add the capture fields¶

Instructions for use already contains the core Article 13 information. Add two optional string fields for logging mechanisms and input-data specification. Optional presence avoids inventing universal requiredness, but it cannot express why information might be relevant. You will preserve that qualification next.

2 · Preserve the qualification¶

A consumer reading required=False learns that a field may be absent. It does not learn that logging information is unnecessary. The selected source says “where relevant”; the application must retain that condition and decide how to use it.

Design the two parts of this contract in the exercise. Then add the descriptive rule through the existing RuleDefinition API. Its statement and evidence will be available outside this notebook; it is not an executable applicability test.

3 · Repair a key without removing the readable fields¶

The provision's document title and provision code are convenient to read, but two editions may share them. The earlier key made an unsafe identity claim. Remove that key and retain the readable attributes. Add the structured locator to carry the edition context.

This is your application's modelling choice, not a new statutory identifier. Removing a key does not remove its attributes, and adding the locator does not automatically create a replacement key.

Your turn: repair identity without erasing useful fields

Two editions may share a document title and provision code. Choose the builder operation that removes that unsafe identity assumption, and what readable information to retain.

  1. Operation on provision-identity: remove_attribute() / remove_key() / remove_concept()
  2. Readable fields after the repair: Keep both readable fields / Delete both fields

Evidence: eli-1. Use the controls below, or write down your answers in the reading version.

Worked answer and explanations

Worked answer

  • remove_key: remove_key() removes the uniqueness claim while retaining the concept and its attributes.
  • keep: Keep the document name and provision code; add the edition-aware locator as a structured field.
builder.remove_key(
    concept=provision,
    key=provision.get_key(name="provision-identity"),
)
# Keep both attributes; add the structured locator next.

The provision retains its identity and readable attributes. The unsafe key is removed and the locator records the edition context; no new uniqueness key is inferred.

async def review_demo_plan(*, workspace: Model, author_plan: ModelChangePlan) -> ReviewCaseId:
    """Submit and explicitly decide the authored plan as the scripted tour reviewer."""
    case = await workspace.propose_change_plan(actor="demo:developer", plan=author_plan)
    if case.status is CaseStatus.PENDING:
        decision = Accept(reason=author_plan.reason)
        _ = await workspace.preview_changes(case=case, decision=decision)
        _ = await workspace.decide_review(actor="demo:reviewer", case=case, decision=decision)
    return case.id


model = await project.get_model(name=model_name)
locator_reason = f"Preserve an edition-aware locator for {article_13.locator}."
locator_plan = await existing_demo_plan(workspace=model, reason=locator_reason)
if locator_plan is None:
    locator_builder = DomainModelBuilder(model_info=model.info)
    locator_builder.add_definition(
        display_name="Provision locator",
        meaning="Identify the source resource, exact edition and within-edition location.",
        body=provision_locator,
    )
    locator_plan = locator_builder.build_change_plan(reason=locator_reason)
_ = await review_demo_plan(workspace=model, author_plan=locator_plan)
inspected_locator = await model.get_definition(name="provision-locator")
_ = sys.stdout.write(f"Reviewed shape: {inspected_locator.name}\n")

4 · Record what still needs human judgement¶

Before review, record the need to inspect the classification qualification. An advisory ManualCriterion makes that responsibility visible without claiming the SDK can prove the interpretation. Its machine result stays UNKNOWN, even after a reviewer agrees with its wording. C8 will distinguish this from a structural defect that the SDK can detect.

Instructions for use

def-instructions-for-use · instructions-for-use · revision 2 · concept

Direct source supportAccepted in this simulated snapshot

Provider-supplied information enabling the deployer to understand the intended purpose and proper use of an AI system. It remains distinct from technical documentation.

Prove you can find the result¶

Put yourself in the consumer developer's place. Use the inspector to find the attribute and the separate rule; enter their lookup names without opening the worked answer. This exercise checks your ability to locate the contract, not just recognise the correct design from a list.

tour.display_practice(exercise_id="c7-handoff")
HANDS-ON PRACTICE

Your turn: find the two objects the consumer needs

Use the refined model inspector above. Enter the lookup name of the optional logging attribute and the separate rule preserving its relevance condition. Enter names, not display labels or IDs.

  1. Attribute lookup name: Enter a lookup name.
  2. Rule lookup name: Enter a lookup name.

Evidence: ai-13-instructions. Use the controls below, or write down your answers in the reading version.

Worked answer and explanations

Worked answer

  • logging-mechanisms: This name resolves the optional string attribute; its generated ID is a separate identity.
  • instructions-logging-information: This name resolves the evidenced descriptive qualification the consumer must retain.
logging = instructions.get_attribute(name="logging-mechanisms")
rule = consumer.get_definition(name="instructions-logging-information")

You found the shape and the separate meaning that must travel with it. In C9 you will retrieve both from an independently loaded bundle.

Optional replay: Change the provision-code attribute display name to Provision reference. Its ID and lookup name should stay the same while the containing definition revision changes. You can also inspect the stale-edit and restore branches after completing the main tasks.

You have turned a reviewed vocabulary into a capture contract while retaining the source qualification and the modelling history. Next, repair a structural blocker and prepare the publication without confusing a human interpretation with a machine check.

Implementation ownership

DK-002, DK-007. Preview completion and SDK acceptance remain separate.

Check your understanding. Which operation made these draft edits part of the accepted model?

Reveal the explanation

The explicit decide_review() submission applied the inspected acceptance. Adding builder operations, building the plan, proposing it and previewing acceptance did not apply the changes. Publication is still a separate operation in C8.

C8 · Resolve and publish¶

You have reviewed the detailed shapes, but one relationship proposal still needs repair. The draft instructions-describe-system refers to an unresolved system identity. It has not entered the accepted model: resolving that endpoint is a structural requirement, not a matter of opinion.

Inspect the rejected draft below, then retrieve the intended system by name and rebuild the relationship with that definition. Preview and accept the repaired proposal. The model gains the connection that the documentation view was missing; no validation requirement is relaxed.

Now record the separate human interpretation of the classification qualification. The advisory manual criterion created in C7 remains advisory and UNKNOWN. Attributed agreement is review evidence, not a machine PASS. You can publish the structurally valid contract while making that limit visible. E1 offers a separate governance experiment about changing a required manual-check policy.

Finally prepare a fresh candidate, inspect its checks and publish 1.1.0. The first publication remains available. You now have both a useful contract and an explanation of how it was reviewed.

Inspect the failed attempt¶

Attempted draft Observed sample result Next action
instructions-describe-system → def-unresolved-system Unresolved target; draft rejected before acceptance Retrieve ai-system and rebuild the relationship
Manual classification interpretation Advisory result remains UNKNOWN Record the reviewer's reason separately

The invalid ID is a deliberate fixture defect, not an ID to paste into your own application. The next planned call uses the returned definition directly. A failed draft changes neither the working model nor an earlier publication.

Deployer log retention

def-deployer-log-retention · deployer-log-retention · revision 1 · rule

Direct source supportAccepted in this simulated snapshot

Deployers retain automatically generated logs to the extent they are under their control, for a period appropriate to purpose and at least six months, unless applicable Union or national law provides otherwise.

Conditions and modelling choices

ElementMeaningBasisEvidence
Responsible actorDeployer of a high-risk AI systemDirect source supportai-26-retention
ActionRetain automatically generated logsDirect source supportai-26-retention
QualificationOnly logs under their controlDirect source supportai-26-retention
DurationAppropriate to intended purpose; at least six monthsDirect source supportai-26-retention
ExceptionApplicable Union or national law may provide otherwiseDirect source supportai-26-retention
Additional qualificationFinancial institutions retain logs within relevant financial-services documentationDirect source supportai-26-retention
RepresentationDescriptive rule inspection, not a new SDK obligation recordApplication-authored choice
Calendar arithmeticNot performed; six months is not converted into a fixed number of daysApplication-authored choice

Inspection annotations on existing descriptive definitions; these conditions are not executable rules.

Source evidence

  • ai-26-retention · Article 26(6); PDF page 68

    Deployers retain automatically generated logs insofar as those logs are under their control. The period must suit the intended purpose and be at least six months, unless applicable Union or national law provides otherwise. Financial institutions have an additional documentation qualification.

C9 · Share the contract¶

You have a published contract with enough detail to be useful outside this notebook. A downstream developer should be able to load it without your workspace connection, inspect instructions for use, discover its references and find the evidence supporting its fields.

Start with the complete bundle, which preserves the SDK's model and review context. Then inspect projections of the same definition. JSON Schema describes supported data shapes; RDF preserves semantic identities; SHACL can describe supported graph shapes; LinkML makes supported schema content available to other tooling. These views have different jobs and are not interchangeable stores.

Pay particular attention to what a projection cannot establish. An optional logging field retains a conditional requirement for interpretation; a valid object does not establish that the underlying documentation is legally adequate. The descriptive classification and retention rules remain useful information, but serializing them does not create a legal reasoning engine.

REVIEWED CONTRACT

logging-mechanisms

Mechanisms for collection, storage and interpretation of logs.

Qualification retained: Where relevant, instructions for use describe the mechanisms that allow deployers to properly collect, store and interpret logs. The optional logging-mechanisms field captures this information; its absence does not establish that the condition is inapplicable.

Published descriptive rule: instructions-logging-information. Direct source support · ifu-logging-mechanisms · revision 2

Curated export expectation: a string property, absent from the root required list. This presentation is not an SDK exporter.

Use the contract without the producer workspace¶

Imagine a second developer receiving the published bundle. They can retrieve instructions for use, inspect the logging field, read the chosen descriptive rules and retain the source citations. Those values can support a documentation form, an extraction target or a catalogue entry in their own application. None of these reads requires the original workspace connection.

The code below reads existing bundle and definition properties. Citation records identify source locations; they do not embed the original documents or fetch them. The richer explanation in the preview also uses our source-ledger teaching annotations. In particular, field-level basis and qualification are not additional public attribute properties.

Start with the logging field, then expand the selector to compare it with the provider reference or the performance-information collection. Notice how the type and presence contract change while the obligation to interpret legal adequacy remains with the host.

You can now test the promise made at the beginning: the logging field is optional in the shape, while instructions-logging-information preserves the relevance condition and Article 13 citation in a published definition. The consumer retrieves both after deserialization. The notebook's extra basis labels and explanations remain teaching annotations; they are not hidden SDK properties.

C10 · Evolve the model¶

Your application will receive more than legislation. A stakeholder paper may argue for a particular approach, clarify an industry concern or challenge an interpretation. It should enrich the evidence available to the application without quietly replacing the meanings derived from the law.

Ingest the real WEC Europe AI-at-work paper as a separately attributed source. In this canonical branch, accept a stakeholder-position concept and its connection to recruitment AI. Compare the resulting publication with versions 1.0.0 and 1.1.0. The counts and definition differences come from the same catalogue as the diagrams; the previously published revisions remain unchanged.

You now have the contract your downstream application can consume: named definitions and shapes, reviewed reference mappings, source evidence, descriptive rules and an attributed version history. The application can use those meanings when it extracts client facts or produces legislative intelligence. Domain Kernel has provided the modelling foundation; this notebook has not built that analysis application.

Inspect a retirement and restoration in the working model¶

Retire the standalone provision locator when the application narrows its inputs. Restore it under the same identity once the edition and within-edition location are in scope again. The scripted decisions leave the earlier shape available in history.

In [47]:
model = await project.get_model(name=model_name)
initial_locator = await model.get_definition(name="provision-locator", revision=1)
retirement_reason = "Temporarily withdraw the locator while the application narrows its inputs."
retirement_plan = await existing_demo_plan(workspace=model, reason=retirement_reason)
if retirement_plan is None:
    retirement_builder = DomainModelBuilder(model_info=model.info)
    retirement_builder.remove_definition(definition=initial_locator)
    retirement_plan = retirement_builder.build_change_plan(reason=retirement_reason)
_ = await review_demo_plan(workspace=model, author_plan=retirement_plan)

model = await project.get_model(name=model_name)
restoration_reason = "Restore the locator after confirming that the edition stays in scope."
restoration_plan = await existing_demo_plan(workspace=model, reason=restoration_reason)
if restoration_plan is None:
    retired_locator = await model.get_definition(name="provision-locator")
    restoration_builder = DomainModelBuilder(model_info=model.info)
    restoration_builder.restore_definition(definition=retired_locator)
    restoration_plan = restoration_builder.build_change_plan(reason=restoration_reason)
restoration_case_id = await review_demo_plan(workspace=model, author_plan=restoration_plan)
locator_history = await model.get_definition_history(definition_id=initial_locator.id)
same_locator = all(item.id == initial_locator.id for item in locator_history.items)
_ = sys.stdout.write(
    f"Locator history: {', '.join(item.status.value for item in locator_history.items)}\n"
    f"Same locator identity: {same_locator}\n"
)

Locator history: approved, retired, approved
Same locator identity: True

Advanced exercises¶

E1 · Formal semantics and LOMO¶

You have seen business mappings that compare meanings. In this branch, examine the stronger claim made by an explicit formal specialisation. The local high-risk recruitment class specialises the recruitment class, which specialises the general AI-system class. A supported RDFS adapter can report the transitive relationship; a business alignment alone would not assert it.

Start from publication 1.1.0 and inspect asserted statements separately from simulated inferences. Compare a small module extraction with an ordinary model view: selecting visible nodes is not a semantic-preservation guarantee. LOMO adds useful legal-rule terminology, but its acquired documentation does not establish that its full ontology and SHACL closure have been loaded.

Implementation ownership

DK-032, DK-034, DK-037, DK-038. Preview completion and SDK acceptance remain separate.

Optional governance branch. Select Review a changed manual-check policy. Start from a copy of 1.1.0 whose governance policy explicitly made a manual criterion REQUIRED. Its UNKNOWN result blocks preparation even when a reviewer agrees with the interpretation. Reviewing a change to ADVISORY changes the release guarantee; it does not prove the statement. Inspect that distinction before applying the separate sample action. The canonical 1.1.0 publication is untouched.

E2 · Reference packs and patterns¶

You have modelled an oversight assignment once. Another project may need the same association between deployer, person and system. Package the reusable meanings and adapt a named pattern instead of copying disconnected snippets.

Start from publication 1.1.0 in a separate design branch. Inspect which identities belong to the reference pack and which become local definitions after adaptation. Then examine a pack replacement that introduces a source obligation. Reuse saves authoring effort, but it must not conceal new review work or invent a suffix when a local name already exists.

E3 · Compose, copy and upgrade models¶

Your recruitment model combines legal metadata, general AI meanings and recruitment-specific definitions. A larger application may share the first two areas across several policy domains. This branch explores how to compose those modules while preserving their original identities and exact version pins.

Start from publication 1.1.0. Compare composition with an independent copy: the copy has its own local identities and lineage, whereas composition retains qualified upstream references. A dependency upgrade then changes a referenced resource, so inspect the coordinated local repair before accepting it. A view is only a way to inspect this content; it does not create another source of truth.

E4 · Profile tables and supplied evidence¶

Not every useful source is a paragraph in a PDF. ELI publishes metadata in a workbook, and your host application may already have extracted text, tables or graph statements from another source. You can retain that work and its original locations rather than parsing it again blindly.

This branch starts from publication 1.1.0 and profiles the explicitly labelled three-row CSV derivative of the real ELI workbook selection. Profiling reports patterns such as nulls, distinct counts and candidate keys; parsing supplies the rows and their locations. Inspect the difference, then replay host-supplied evidence against its recorded source identity.

E5 · Record and confirm a clarification¶

A source cannot explain every application-design choice. Your modelling colleague can clarify that a provision code is a local locator rather than a statutory identifier. Capture that statement with its speaker, recorder and time so the distinction is reviewable later.

Start from publication 1.1.0. The fictional colleague and statement are labelled examples, not quotations from an actual policymaker. Recording the statement is separate from confirming it; confirmation is also separate from changing a definition. Inspect each boundary before submitting the sample confirmation.

E6 · Rich shapes and languages¶

You now know why an instructions field can be optional even though a legal condition may make it necessary in a particular case. This branch explores the rest of the shape vocabulary: field presence, nulls, ordered lists, distinct sets, bounds and open vocabularies.

Start from publication 1.1.0 in a copied design. Extend the edition-aware provision locator and inspect the source-verified French labels for the general AI system, provider and deployer. Do not attach the general statutory French label to the narrower recruitment concept as though the meanings were identical. The child-edit alternatives remain unsubmitted until you inspect and choose one.

Live SDK · Author an actor-role assignment. Inspect a local assignment key, a closed list of roles, and an open vocabulary of recruitment uses. Apply the verified Article 3 labels to the general system and actor roles. The IDs below identify captured in-memory drafts for authoring. The following plan persists the authored assignment and its vocabularies.

In [54]:
shape_scope = ModelScope(
    project_id=ProjectId(value="tour-draft"), model_id=ModelId(value="recruitment-shapes")
)
french_edition = next(record for record in load_sources() if record.id == "ai-act-fr")
french_labels = next(record for record in french_edition.passages if record.id == "ai-fr-3")
system_fr, provider_fr, deployer_fr = french_labels.text.split("; ")


def actor_terminology(*, english: str, french: str) -> Terminology:
    """Capture the source-checked labels for one general statutory meaning."""
    return Terminology(
        labels=[
            LocalizedLabel(text=LabelText(value=english), language=LanguageTag(value="en")),
            LocalizedLabel(text=LabelText(value=french), language=LanguageTag(value="fr")),
        ],
    )


system = Concept(
    id=DefinitionId(value="ai-system"),
    scope=shape_scope,
    revision=1,
    name="ai-system",
    display_name="AI system",
    meaning="The general AI-system meaning in Article 3(1).",
    terminology=actor_terminology(english="AI system", french=system_fr),
    body=ConceptDefinition(),
)
roles = Definition(
    id=DefinitionId(value="actor-roles"),
    scope=shape_scope,
    revision=1,
    name="actor-roles",
    display_name="Actor roles",
    meaning="Roles recorded by this application for an AI system.",
    body=ValueSetDefinition(
        membership=ValueSetMembership.CLOSED,
        members=[
            ValueSetMember(
                code=BusinessCode(value="provider"),
                label=LabelText(value="Provider"),
                meaning=MeaningText(value="The provider role for the selected system."),
                terminology=actor_terminology(english="Provider", french=provider_fr),
            ),
            ValueSetMember(
                code=BusinessCode(value="deployer"),
                label=LabelText(value="Deployer"),
                meaning=MeaningText(value="The deployer role for the selected system."),
                terminology=actor_terminology(english="Deployer", french=deployer_fr),
            ),
        ],
    ),
)
uses = Definition(
    id=DefinitionId(value="recruitment-uses"),
    scope=shape_scope,
    revision=1,
    name="recruitment-uses",
    display_name="Recruitment uses",
    meaning="Known application categories for recording recruitment uses.",
    body=ValueSetDefinition(
        membership=ValueSetMembership.OPEN,
        members=[
            ValueSetMember(
                code=BusinessCode(value="application-screening"),
                label=LabelText(value="Application screening"),
                meaning=MeaningText(value="Screening or filtering applications."),
            ),
        ],
    ),
)
assignment_code = AttributeDefinition.string(
    display_name="Application assignment code", required=True
)
assignment_key = KeyDefinition(
    display_name="Application assignment key", attributes=[assignment_code.id]
)
assignment = Concept(
    id=DefinitionId(value="actor-role-assignment"),
    scope=shape_scope,
    revision=1,
    name="actor-role-assignment",
    display_name="Actor role assignment",
    meaning="Relate an application actor code, its role and a selected AI system.",
    body=ConceptDefinition(
        attributes=[
            assignment_code,
            AttributeDefinition.string(display_name="Application actor code", required=True),
            AttributeDefinition.reference(
                target=system.id, display_name="AI system", required=True
            ),
            AttributeDefinition.value_set(value_set=roles.id, display_name="Role", required=True),
            AttributeDefinition.value_set(
                value_set=uses.id,
                display_name="Related recruitment uses",
                collection=CollectionKind.SET,
                min_items=Count(value=1),
                max_items=Count(value=4),
            ),
        ],
        keys=[assignment_key],
    ),
)
related_uses = assignment.get_attribute(name="related-recruitment-uses")
assignment_fields = ", ".join(field.name for field in assignment.attributes)
role_codes = ", ".join(member.code.value for member in roles.body.members)
_ = sys.stdout.write(
    f"{assignment.display_name} fields {assignment_fields}\n"
    f"Local key {assignment.get_key(name='application-assignment-key').name}\n"
    f"{roles.body.membership.value.title()} roles {role_codes}\n"
    f"{uses.body.membership.value.title()} recruitment uses allow new codes\n"
    f"Optional set allows {related_uses.min_items.value} to "
    f"{related_uses.max_items.value} when present\n"
    f"Article 3 French labels {french_labels.text}\n"
)

model = await project.get_model(name=model_name)
assignment_reason = "Preserve the roles, local key and vocabulary bounds for actor assignments."
assignment_plan = await existing_demo_plan(workspace=model, reason=assignment_reason)
if assignment_plan is None:
    assignment_builder = DomainModelBuilder(model_info=model.info)
    general_system_id = assignment_builder.add_concept(
        name=system.name,
        display_name=system.display_name,
        meaning=system.meaning,
        terminology=system.terminology,
    )
    roles_id = assignment_builder.add_value_set(
        name=roles.name,
        display_name=roles.display_name,
        meaning=roles.meaning,
        membership=roles.body.membership,
        members=roles.body.members,
    )
    uses_id = assignment_builder.add_value_set(
        name=uses.name,
        display_name=uses.display_name,
        meaning=uses.meaning,
        membership=uses.body.membership,
        members=uses.body.members,
    )
    assignment_builder.add_concept(
        display_name=assignment.display_name,
        meaning=assignment.meaning,
        keys=[assignment_key],
        attributes=[
            assignment_code,
            assignment.get_attribute(name="application-actor-code"),
            AttributeDefinition.reference(
                target=general_system_id, display_name="AI system", required=True
            ),
            AttributeDefinition.value_set(value_set=roles_id, display_name="Role", required=True),
            AttributeDefinition.value_set(
                value_set=uses_id,
                display_name="Related recruitment uses",
                collection=CollectionKind.SET,
                min_items=Count(value=1),
                max_items=Count(value=4),
            ),
        ],
    )
    assignment_plan = assignment_builder.build_change_plan(reason=assignment_reason)
_ = await review_demo_plan(workspace=model, author_plan=assignment_plan)
reviewed_assignment = await model.get_concept(name=assignment.name)
_ = sys.stdout.write(
    f"Reviewed assignment: {reviewed_assignment.name}\n"
    f"Persisted key: {reviewed_assignment.get_key(name=assignment_key.name).name}\n"
)

model = await project.get_model(name=model_name)
reviewed_assignment = await model.get_concept(name="actor-role-assignment")
child_edit_reason = "Allow an empty set of related uses while keeping the assignment key."
child_edit_plan = await existing_demo_plan(workspace=model, reason=child_edit_reason)
if child_edit_plan is None:
    child_builder = DomainModelBuilder(model_info=model.info)
    child_builder.edit_attribute(
        concept=reviewed_assignment,
        attribute=reviewed_assignment.get_attribute(name="related-recruitment-uses"),
        min_items=None,
    )
    child_builder.edit_key(
        concept=reviewed_assignment,
        key=reviewed_assignment.get_key(name="application-assignment-key"),
        display_name="Application assignment identity",
    )
    child_edit_plan = child_builder.build_change_plan(reason=child_edit_reason)
_ = await review_demo_plan(workspace=model, author_plan=child_edit_plan)
before_assignment = await model.get_concept(name="actor-role-assignment", revision=1)
after_assignment = await model.get_concept(name="actor-role-assignment")
old_uses = before_assignment.get_attribute(name="related-recruitment-uses")
new_uses = after_assignment.get_attribute(name="related-recruitment-uses")
_ = sys.stdout.write(
    f"Related uses minimum: {old_uses.min_items.value} to {new_uses.min_items.value}\n"
    f"Same attribute ID: {old_uses.id == new_uses.id}\n"
    f"Reviewed key label: {after_assignment.keys[0].display_name}\n"
)

E7 · Describe processes and decisions¶

A domain model can describe activities as well as entities. Article 9 describes an iterative risk-management process: identify and evaluate risks, consider monitoring information and select measures. Represent a small illustrative iteration so a downstream application can understand those activities and their roles.

Start from publication 1.1.0. This is a process described by the domain, not the SDK's own review workflow. Its sequence is an authored teaching structure rather than a claim that the Act prescribes a single workflow. Inspect the classification decision definition alongside it: both are descriptions, and neither executes a case or schedules work.

E8 · Inspect interoperability boundaries¶

Another team may arrive with a schema instead of prose. Import a bounded LinkML description of instructions for use and compare its class and slots with the definitions you already published. Existing local names require an explicit review decision; importing a file must not create a second competing meaning automatically.

Start from publication 1.1.0. Inspect the proposal and diagnostic boundaries before accepting anything. Keep ontology declarations, model metadata, model-validation shapes and downstream instance shapes separate. A supported schema round-trip does not imply that descriptive legal conditions round-trip as executable logic.

recruitment-activityconcept / 1An activity in recruitment or selection; its category describes intended use without deciding legal classification.Inferred modelling structureai-annex-recruitment
legal-provisionconcept / 2An addressable article, paragraph or annex item in a specific legislative resource.Inferred modelling structureeli-1
ai-systemconcept / 1A machine-based system with varying autonomy and possible adaptiveness that infers from input how to generate outputs capable of influencing physical or virtual environments.Direct source supportai-3-system
high-risk-recruitment-ai-systemconcept / 1A recruitment AI system classified as high-risk under Article 6, preserving the qualification and profiling provision in Article 6(3).Inferred modelling structureai-annex-recruitment, ai-6-classification
intended-purposeconcept / 1The provider-specified intended use, including context and conditions described in supplied information.Direct source supportai-3-purpose
candidateconcept / 1A natural person being considered in recruitment or selection; no statutory candidate identifier or scoring scale is assumed.Inferred modelling structureai-annex-recruitment
job-applicationconcept / 1Information submitted for consideration in recruitment; its detailed record schema is left to the consuming application.Inferred modelling structureai-annex-recruitment
job-advertisementconcept / 1A communication advertising a job opportunity, including the targeted advertising use mentioned in Annex III.Inferred modelling structureai-annex-recruitment
candidate-evaluationconcept / 1An assessment of a candidate in recruitment or selection; the model does not prescribe a numerical scoring method.Inferred modelling structureai-annex-recruitment
natural-personconcept / 1A human individual, distinguished from an organisation or legal-person role.Inferred modelling structureai-3-actors, ai-26-oversight
oversight-assignmentconcept / 1An application-modelled association between a deployer, a natural person and a system to which oversight responsibility is assigned.Inferred modelling structureai-26-oversight
instructions-for-useconcept / 2Provider-supplied information enabling the deployer to understand the intended purpose and proper use of an AI system. It remains distinct from technical documentation.Direct source supportai-3-purpose, ai-13-instructions
technical-documentationconcept / 1Documentation prepared before placing a high-risk system on the market or putting it into service, maintained to support assessment of requirements; its minimum content is specified in Annex IV.Direct source supportai-11-documentation
performance-informationstructured_value / 1A reusable structure for reported performance metrics and the circumstances in which they apply. The Act does not supply universal metric names or thresholds.Inferred modelling structureai-13-instructions
datasetconcept / 1A collection of data described separately from its role in training, validation, testing or operation; Article 10 and deployer-controlled input data have distinct scopes.Inferred modelling structureai-10-data, ai-26-oversight
automatically-generated-logconcept / 1An event record automatically generated by an AI system. This model describes the record type; hosts manage actual logs.Direct source supportai-12-logs
human-oversight-measureconcept / 1A technical or organisational measure enabling effective human oversight, built into the system or identified for deployer implementation.Direct source supportai-14-oversight
riskconcept / 1The combination of probability of harm and its severity, considered in the intended-use and foreseeable-misuse context.Inferred modelling structureai-3-risk, ai-9-risk
mitigation-measureconcept / 1A measure selected to address an identified risk through design, controls or information, retaining its rationale and context.Inferred modelling structureai-9-risk
legal-resourceconcept / 1A legal resource identified independently of its language expression and document format.Direct source supporteli-1
classification-assessmentconcept / 1A documented assessment of a system against the applicable high-risk classification conditions. Recording an assessment is not SDK adjudication.Inferred modelling structureai-6-classification

E9 · Recover and change deployment¶

A real discovery workload will encounter interruptions, remote permissions and more review cases than fit on one page. You should be able to recover the unfinished work without repeating completed segments or treating an empty result page as success.

Use the larger instructions, dataset and oversight proposal groups in a separate branch from publication 1.1.0. Inspect the simulated checkpoint, per-source failure and next cursor. Then compare local and optional PostgreSQL configuration. An unavailable configured backend must fail explicitly; it must not silently create a different SQLite workspace.

Use the C1 demo workspace name after a restart. A new client can load the same project and model IDs from SQLite. DK-007 and DK-009 add durable revision and publication history. The SQLite conformance tests exercise reopening, and the audit tests exercise committed history and coordinated rollback. The checkpoint below is a simulated result.

In [61]:
reopened_client = Client(config=ClientConfiguration(base_dir=demo_workspace))
reopened_project = await reopened_client.get_project(name=project_name)
reopened_model = await reopened_project.get_model(name=model_name)
_ = sys.stdout.write(
    f"Reopened: {reopened_model.info.name}\n"
    f"Same project and model IDs: {reopened_model.scope == model.scope}\n"
)

Reopened: ai-in-recruitment
Same project and model IDs: True

restoration_decision = restoration_history.items[0]
_ = sys.stdout.write(

    f"Restored name: {restoration_decision.applied_changes.changes[0].after[0].name}\n"

E10 · Inspect the notebook experience¶

You have used the notebook as a teaching tool, but it is also where you will inspect the SDK while developing it. Test whether the result remains understandable when the model grows, a definition is outside the selected diagram, or no live widget kernel is available.

Start from publication 1.1.0. Search for instructions, switch to a safeguards view and inspect the same definition's evidence. These controls read loaded records only. Changing a review decision invalidates its earlier impact preview, while merely displaying a model never creates a decision. The static diagrams, tables and saved definition cards provide equivalent reading material.

R1 · Reusable units and numeric detail¶

Some application data needs a magnitude and unit rather than an unqualified number. This recipe models a processing duration in hours, using a reusable SDK-authored unit without requiring an ontology term. The examples show what a supported quantity shape can validate.

Start from publication 1.1.0 in an isolated branch. A processing duration is an application choice, distinct from the Act's retention periods. In particular, the descriptive six-month retention rule is not converted into a fixed number of hours or days. Unit conversion, rounding and calendar arithmetic remain explicit downstream responsibilities.

Live SDK · Capture processing duration. Reference a reusable hour from the closed duration vocabulary. Pair a required decimal magnitude with a required unit. A separate decimal field records the application's desired precision and scale for data collection.

In [65]:
hour = Definition(
    id=DefinitionId(value="hour"),
    scope=shape_scope,
    revision=1,
    name="hour",
    display_name="Hour",
    meaning="The local processing duration unit.",
    body=UnitDefinition(symbol="h"),
)
duration_units = Definition(
    id=DefinitionId(value="duration-units"),
    scope=shape_scope,
    revision=1,
    name="processing-duration-units",
    display_name="Processing duration units",
    meaning="Permitted processing duration unit codes.",
    body=ValueSetDefinition(
        membership=ValueSetMembership.CLOSED,
        members=[
            ValueSetMember(
                code=BusinessCode(value="h"),
                label=LabelText(value="Hour"),
                meaning=MeaningText(value="An hour of processing time."),
                unit=hour.id,
            ),
        ],
    ),
)
magnitude = AttributeDefinition.decimal(display_name="Magnitude", required=True)
unit_field = AttributeDefinition.value_set(
    display_name="Unit",
    value_set=duration_units.id,
    required=True,
)
duration = StructuredValueDefinition(
    attributes=[magnitude, unit_field],
    quantity=QuantityBinding(magnitude=magnitude.id, unit=unit_field.id),
)
measured_facets = DecimalFacets(precision=DecimalPrecision(value=8), scale=DecimalScale(value=2))
measured_duration = AttributeDefinition.decimal(
    display_name="Measured duration",
    required=True,
    facets=measured_facets,
)
duration_fields = ", ".join(field.name for field in duration.attributes if field.required)
_ = sys.stdout.write(
    f"Processing duration requires {duration_fields}\n"
    f"{duration_units.body.membership.value.title()} unit code "
    f"{duration_units.body.members[0].code.value} references reusable {hour.display_name}\n"
    f"{measured_duration.display_name} uses precision {measured_facets.precision.value} "
    f"and scale {measured_facets.scale.value}\n"
)

Processing duration requires magnitude, unit
Closed unit code h references reusable Hour
Measured duration uses precision 8 and scale 2
In [66]:
model = await project.get_model(name=model_name)
duration_reason = "Review the processing duration with its reusable local hour."
duration_plan = await existing_demo_plan(workspace=model, reason=duration_reason)
if duration_plan is None:
    duration_builder = DomainModelBuilder(model_info=model.info)
    hour_id = duration_builder.add_unit(
        display_name="Hour",
        meaning="The local processing duration unit.",
        symbol="h",
    )
    units_id = duration_builder.add_value_set(
        display_name="Processing duration units",
        meaning="Permitted processing duration codes.",
        membership=ValueSetMembership.CLOSED,
        members=[
            ValueSetMember(
                code=BusinessCode(value="h"),
                label=LabelText(value="Hour"),
                meaning=MeaningText(value="An hour of processing time."),
                unit=hour_id,
            ),
        ],
    )
    duration_builder.add_quantity(
        display_name="Processing duration",
        meaning="A required elapsed-time magnitude and approved unit.",
        units=units_id,
    )
    duration_plan = duration_builder.build_change_plan(reason=duration_reason)
_ = await review_demo_plan(workspace=model, author_plan=duration_plan)
reviewed_hour = await model.get_unit(name="hour")
reviewed_duration = await model.get_definition(name="processing-duration")
_ = sys.stdout.write(
    f"Reviewed duration: {reviewed_duration.name}\n"
    f"Reusable unit: {reviewed_hour.name} ({reviewed_hour.body.symbol})\n"
)

Reviewed duration: processing-duration
Reusable unit: hour (h)

Source ledger and selected passages¶

The legal baseline is the original 2024 Official Journal edition, not a claim about the law currently in force. English and French original PDF bytes were acquired and hashed; selected passages were checked against those PDFs. The evidence below identifies its actual representation and distinguishes paraphrases from quotations. Parser and inference results remain simulated.

Official legislation, Commission guidance and stakeholder opinion have different authority. Ontologies are independent reference resources. An acquired documentation page does not establish a complete ontology or SHACL dependency closure. Original documents are linked rather than redistributed; fixtures/acquisition.json records acquisition details.

AI Act¶

Classification: Legislation Edition: Regulation (EU) 2024/1689 • original OJ edition, 12 July 2024 • EN

Open source

Verification: Official original OJ PDF acquired; 144 pages; edition and selected passages checked against extracted PDF text. Parser and inference results below remain simulated.

Original-byte SHA-256: bba630444b3278e881066774002a1d7824308934f49ccfa203e65be43692f55e

Attribution: European Union. Official source linked; no full original redistributed.

  • ai-3-system · Article 3(1); PDF page 46 — Source-checked paraphrase

    The system definition combines machine-based operation, varying autonomy, possible adaptiveness and inference from inputs to outputs that can influence environments.

  • ai-3-actors · Article 3(3)–(4); PDF page 46 — Source-checked paraphrase

    Provider covers developing or commissioning a system and placing it on the market or putting it into service under an own name or trademark. Deployer concerns use under own authority, excluding personal non-professional activity.

  • ai-3-purpose · Article 3(12), (15), (23); PDF page 47 — Source-checked paraphrase

    Intended purpose includes the provider-specified use, context and conditions. Instructions inform deployers about purpose and proper use. Substantial modification is separately defined.

  • ai-annex-recruitment · Annex III(4)(a); PDF page 127 — Source-checked paraphrase

    The listed recruitment and selection uses include targeted job advertising, analysis and filtering of applications, and evaluation of candidates. The list must be read with Article 6.

  • ai-6-classification · Article 6(2)–(4); PDF pages 53–54 — Source-checked paraphrase

    Annex III systems are classified as high-risk, subject to the paragraph 3 qualification concerning significant risk and the specified procedural, improvement, pattern-detection or preparatory tasks. Annex III profiling systems remain high-risk. A provider concluding that a system is not high-risk must document its assessment before market placement or service and comply with the stated registration obligation.

  • ai-9-risk · Article 9(1)–(5); PDF page 56 — Source-checked paraphrase

    Risk management is a documented, maintained, continuous lifecycle process. It identifies and evaluates foreseeable risks and misuse, considers monitoring information, and adopts appropriate measures. Risk is not just a single score.

  • ai-10-data · Article 10(1)–(4), (6); PDF pages 57–58 — Source-checked paraphrase

    Training, validation and testing datasets have distinct roles. Governance covers origin, preparation, assumptions, suitability, bias and data gaps. Quality is assessed in view of intended purpose; paragraph 6 limits these requirements to testing datasets for systems not using model-training techniques.

  • ai-11-documentation · Article 11(1); PDF page 58 — Source-checked paraphrase

    Technical documentation is prepared before market placement or service, kept current, and supports assessment against the high-risk requirements. Annex IV specifies its minimum content.

  • ai-12-logs · Article 12(1)–(2); PDF page 59 — Source-checked paraphrase

    High-risk systems provide automatic event recording to support traceability, monitoring and identification of risks or substantial modifications. The additional biometric-specific fields in paragraph 3 are not general recruitment requirements.

  • ai-13-instructions · Article 13(2)–(3); PDF pages 59–60 — Source-checked paraphrase

    Instructions identify the provider and explain purpose, capabilities, limitations, tested performance, foreseeable risks and oversight. They also describe relevant maintenance and logging arrangements. Several information items are qualified by applicability, appropriateness or relevance.

  • ai-14-oversight · Article 14(3)–(4); PDF pages 60–61 — Source-checked paraphrase

    Oversight measures may be built into a system or identified for implementation by the deployer. As appropriate and proportionate, assigned people can understand limitations, monitor, interpret outputs, avoid automation bias, override outputs and interrupt operation.

  • ai-25-roles · Article 25(1)–(2); PDF page 67 — Source-checked paraphrase

    Specified changes to branding, substantial modification or intended purpose can transfer provider responsibilities for a particular system. The conditions and qualifications must remain attached to that role change.

  • ai-26-oversight · Article 26(1)–(4); PDF pages 67–68 — Source-checked paraphrase

    Deployers use high-risk systems according to instructions and assign oversight to natural persons with competence, training, authority and support. Relevant, representative input data is required insofar as the deployer controls that data.

  • ai-26-retention · Article 26(6); PDF page 68 — Source-checked paraphrase

    Deployers retain automatically generated logs insofar as those logs are under their control. The period must suit the intended purpose and be at least six months, unless applicable Union or national law provides otherwise. Financial institutions have an additional documentation qualification.

  • ai-3-risk · Article 3(2); PDF page 46 — Source-checked paraphrase

    Risk combines the probability of harm occurring and the severity of that harm.
